Caroline, Paul —

Thanks for the details. A few engineering notes to guide the sizing conversation:

- Token profile you shared (avg 180 / 80) and the 6-turn sessions imply a significant KV cache benefit. With prefix caching you can reduce per-request compute by ~25-40% depending on prompt reuse.
- For 120 TPS peak (assuming 60% short, 30% multi-turn, 10% embeddings):
  * Baseline estimated token throughput: ~15M tokens/minute aggregate (back-of-envelope).
  * Concurrency per request path: we typically run multi-turn sessions on lower-latency nodes to keep tail P95 < 200ms for short queries.

GPU guidance (tradeoffs):
- H100 (best perf): smaller cluster size, best single-token throughput, recommended if you must hit tight p95 SLAs and will use FP16 / no quantization. More expensive but fewer GPUs required.
- A100 (balanced): good for mixed workloads, strong memory for long context, recommended if you expect longer sessions and want flexibility.
- L4 / T4 class (cost-efficient): viable if you accept higher latency and plan aggressive 8-bit quantization / larger batching.

Sizing starting point (conservative):
- Option A (Aggressive latency): 6x H100 (n1) in a reserved pool — targets 120 TPS with low p95 and headroom for growth.
- Option B (Balanced): 12x A100 (n1) — better memory headroom for multi-turn and embeddings.
- Option C (Cost-first): 20x L4-equivalent with heavy batching and quantization (higher latency variability).

We'll prepare a capacity worksheet with per-option estimated QPS, token/sec, expected p95, and cost rates. Happy to run a short quality check if you want to exercise quantized weights against your prompts.
